actions.title: Action 1. Establish Multilevel Commitments and Platforms for Climate Investment
paragraphs: Brazil has strengthened national–subnational climate coordination through its [Commitment to Climate Federalism](https://ses.sp.bvs.br/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/U_RS-PR-CF-3_030724.pdf), adopted in 2024, and its [Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)](https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/2024-11/Brazil_Second%20Nationally%20Determined%20Contribution%20%28NDC%29_November2024.pdf), which recognizes states and municipalities as essential implementation partners. The Interministerial Committee on Climate Change (CIM), supported by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MMA), coordinates federal climate policy, while its Interfederative Coordination Chamber provides a mechanism for state and municipal participation. The [Green and Resilient Cities Programme (PCVR)](https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/assuntos/meio-ambiente-urbano-recursos-hidricos-qualidade-ambiental/cidades-verdes-resilientes/Banco%20de%20Projetos%20do%20Programa%20Cidades%20Verdes%20e%20Resilientes/banco-de-projetos-do-programa-cidades-verdes-e-resilientes-pcvr), jointly governed by MMA, the Ministry of Cities and the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI), provides a dedicated framework for coordinating urban climate action across federal institutions and government levels. Notably, PCVR does not have its own financial resources and operates through repayable financing from Fundo Clima and the Pró-Cidades Programme.

Municipal associations also contribute to multilevel coordination. The National Front of Mayors (FNP) facilitates national–subnational dialogue on climate governance and investment priorities, including through its [Climate Federalism letter presented at COP30](https://fnp.org.br/noticias/item/3679-carta-da-fnp-sobre-federalismo-climatico-e-entregue-ao-presidente-lula-na-cop-30) and [federative dialogue on climate governance](https://fnp.org.br/noticias/item/3910-dialogo-federativo-debate-caminhos-para-fortalecer-a-governanca-climatica-no-brasil).

Brazil is also developing broader national investment coordination and investments mechanisms. The [Brazil Investment Platform (BIP)](https://www.gov.br/fazenda/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/acoes-e-programas/transformacao-ecologica/bip), led by the Ministry of Finance with BNDES as Secretariat, brings national institutions and financing partners together around climate-aligned investment opportunities. BIP is focused on mitigation projects and does not currently cover adaptation projects. While it provides an important national coordination and finance-mobilization function, systematic municipal participation and links with urban project pipelines remain to be established.
Additionally, partner-led initiatives, including the Brazil CHAMP Finance Working Group, provide further opportunities to connect institutions working on local climate finance.
actions.enabledSummary: What this has enabled: Brazil has established political commitments and institutional mechanisms for multilevel climate coordination, alongside emerging national investment platforms. The opportunity is to strengthen connections between municipal investment priorities and national financing decisions.

actions.title: Action 2. Strengthen Enabling Environments for Climate Investment
paragraphs: Brazil has established national mechanisms to assess and improve the fiscal conditions affecting municipal investment. The National Treasury's [CAPAG framework](https://www.tesourotransparente.gov.br/temas/estados-e-municipios/capacidade-de-pagamento-capag) assesses municipal creditworthiness based on indebtedness, current savings and liquidity, influencing eligibility for federally guaranteed borrowing. Building on these assessments, the [Fiscal Balance Promotion Plan (PEF)](https://www.tesourotransparente.gov.br/temas/estados-e-municipios/plano-de-promocao-do-equilibrio-fiscal-pef) enables eligible states and municipalities with weaker creditworthiness to undertake agreed fiscal reforms and meet performance targets in exchange for access to federally guaranteed loans.

Brazil also supports municipal institutional strengthening through the [National Programme for Administrative and Fiscal Management of Brazilian Municipalities (PNAFM)](https://www.gov.br/fazenda/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/acoes-e-programas/pnafm), which provides financing for improvements in local revenue administration, budgeting and financial management. While these programmes are not specifically designed for climate investment, they address underlying fiscal and institutional barriers affecting municipalities' ability to finance and implement infrastructure projects. Additionally, the Brazil CHAMP Finance Working Group is a partner-led coordination forum bringing together international and national partners to align programmes, exchange knowledge and strengthen coordination of support for municipal climate finance and implementation.
actions.enabledSummary: What this has enabled: Brazil has established fiscal assessment, reform incentives and institutional strengthening mechanisms that can improve municipal investment conditions. The opportunity is to connect these mechanisms more explicitly with urban and subnational climate finance needs.

actions.title: Action 3. Plan and Prepare Climate Investments
paragraphs:
Brazil has established federal infrastructure investment programmes along with newer mechanisms for identifying municipal climate investment needs. Through [Novo PAC](https://www.gov.br/cidades/pt-br/novo-pac-selecoes), states and municipalities can submit infrastructure investment proposals for federal support, including projects in sustainable mobility, sanitation and disaster prevention. More recently, the [PCVR Project Bank](https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/assuntos/meio-ambiente-urbano-recursos-hidricos-qualidade-ambiental/cidades-verdes-resilientes/Banco%20de%20Projetos%20do%20Programa%20Cidades%20Verdes%20e%20Resilientes/banco-de-projetos-do-programa-cidades-verdes-e-resilientes-pcvr), developed by MMA with Cities Climate Finance Leadership Alliance (CCFLA) and the University of Brasília, has begun consolidating municipal and state climate project proposals. It helps map investment demand, identify preparation gaps and improve project visibility to technical assistance and financing partners.
Additionally, the [Infrastructure Support Fund for Recovery and Adaptation to Extreme Climate Events (FIRECE)](https://www.gov.br/casacivil/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/fundos/fundo-de-apoio-a-infraestrutura-para-recuperacao-e-adaptacao-a-eventos-climaticos-extremos) supports the planning and implementation of resilience infrastructure. Its first implementation plan covers eight areas of intervention for infrastructure recovery, disaster prevention and adaptation in the Porto Alegre Metropolitan Region and surrounding areas. The planned works directly benefit 16 municipalities, with additional studies and projects envisaged for future interventions in the Caí Basin.

Complementary initiatives are strengthening municipal access to project preparation support. The **[Brazil Mutirão Programme](https://www.c40.org/news/brazil-c40-cities-and-the-global-covenant-of-mayors-announce-new-mutirao-effort-to-accelerate-urban-climate-solutions-in-brazil/)**, launched by C40 Cities and the Global Covenant of Mayors with support from Bloomberg Philanthropies and facilitation by the National Front of Mayors (FNP), supports cities with climate budgeting, project preparation and financial structuring. In March 2026, [34 municipalities and two states](https://www.c40.org/news/brazil-announces-more-than-30-cities-and-regions-will-accelerate-climate-action-projects-through-mutirao-program/) were selected for support. ICLEI's **[Transformative Actions Program (TAP Brasil)](https://americadosul.iclei.org/en/brazil/project/tap-brazil-program-of-transformative-actions/)** similarly provides technical assistance, training and mentoring to help subnational governments develop investable climate projects and engage potential funders. The **[C40 Cities Finance Facility (CFF)](https://www.c40.org/c40-cities-finance-facility/), **jointly implemented by C40 Cities and GIZ, has also supported project preparation in Brazilian cities, including [Curitiba's Caximba solar project](https://www.c40.org/news/curitiba-from-landfill-to-solar-revolution/), which became operational in 2023. More recently, [Belo Horizonte and São Paulo were selected for CFF support in 2025](https://www.c40.org/news/belo-horizonte-sao-paulo-rabat-and-cartagena-to-receive-funding-boost-for-new-climate-projects/). The facility provides technical assistance through feasibility studies, financial modelling and engagement with potential financiers.
actions.enabledSummary: Brazil’s federal and partner-led programs are improving the visibility of municipal climate investment pipelines and expanding project preparation support. The opportunity is to connect these initiatives more systematically with national financing institutions and programmes, helping projects progress from identification to investment readiness and financing.

actions.title: Action 4. Mobilize Finance and Shape Markets
paragraphs: Brazil has an established public financing architecture for urban infrastructure, complemented by dedicated climate finance instruments. [Novo PAC](https://www.gov.br/cidades/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/acoes-e-programas/pac) supports eligible state and municipal investments through federal transfers and credit, including FGTS-backed financing, while BNDES and CAIXA provide established financing channels. The Ministry of Cities also oversees [Pró-Cidades](https://www.gov.br/cidades/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/perguntas-frequentes/desenvolvimento-regional), an FGTS-backed credit programme supporting eligible urban development investments. Additionally, the National Climate Fund (Fundo Clima), coordinated by MMA and operated through BNDES for repayable financing, has expanded its support for climate-related investments, including urban resilience and mobility.

[FIRECE](https://www.gov.br/casacivil/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/fundos/fundo-de-apoio-a-infraestrutura-para-recuperacao-e-adaptacao-a-eventos-climaticos-extremos) provides a complementary federal financing instrument for infrastructure recovery and adaptation to extreme climate events. Managed by CAIXA, with governance involving Casa Civil (the Office of the Chief of Staff of the Presidency), the Ministry of Cities and the Ministry of Finance, the fund received approximately R$6.5 billion in December 2024 to support resilience infrastructure investments following the Rio Grande do Sul floods.

More recent finance-mobilization initiatives include the Brazil Investment Platform (BIP, discussed under Action 1) along with [Eco Invest Brasil](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/lei/l14995.htm), which uses concessional finance and currency-risk mitigation to attract private capital. By January 2026, BIP had incorporated [17 projects representing approximately USD 25 billion](https://www.gov.br/fazenda/pt-br/central-de-conteudo/publicacoes/relatorios/sain/relatorio-de-gestao-da-sain-2023-2026.pdf) in potential investment and facilitated more than 80 project–financier connections. Alongside these national initiatives, the [Global Innovation Lab for Climate Finance's Brazil programme](https://www.climatefinancelab.org/network/brazil/), supported by Climate Policy Initiative, brings public and private actors together to develop innovative climate financing instruments.
actions.enabledSummary: Brazil has multiple channels for mobilizing public, development and private finance, alongside new frameworks for strategic sustainable procurement. The opportunity is to connect some of these financing and market-shaping mechanisms more closely with municipal investment pipelines, financing barriers and procurement needs.

actions.title: Action 5. Learn, Strengthen Capacities and Scale Implementation
paragraphs: Brazil has developed experience in combining federal programmes, international partnerships and local implementation to test urban sustainability approaches. **[CITinova – Integrated Sustainable Cities](https://www.thegef.org/projects-operations/projects/9142)**, led by MCTI and implemented with UNEP and national and local partners, combined integrated urban planning with pilot investments in sustainable technologies in Brasília and Recife between 2018 and 2022. Supported by approximately [USD 23 million in GEF grants and USD 195 million in co-financing](https://climaesociedade.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/REPOSITIONING-BRAZIL-AS-A-GLOBAL-HUB-FOR-CLIMATE-SOLUTIONS.pdf), the programme demonstrated how national institutions, international partners and local governments could coordinate planning and implementation. Its successor[, CITinova](https://www.funbio.org.br/en/programas_e_projetos/rio-doce-biodiversity-2/) II, builds on this experience through metropolitan coordination, demonstration projects and partnerships with financing institutions.

Institutional capacity building is also advancing through [AdaptaCidades](https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/composicao/smc/adaptacidades-1), coordinated by MMA under PCVR. The initiative supports states and municipalities with climate-risk information, technical guidance, mentoring and training for local adaptation planning, alongside guidance on accessing finance. Its initial programme design prioritises support for 260 municipalities, working through state governments and, where appropriate, intermunicipal arrangements.

The Ministry of Cities also supports municipal institutional capacity building through the [National Cities Capacity Building Programme (Capacidades)](https://www.capacidades.gov.br/), which provides training and learning resources on urban development and climate-related issues. Additionally, Ministry of Cities’ [Projeto AdaptAÇÃO](https://www.gov.br/cidades/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/acoes-e-programas/desenvolvimento-urbano-e-metropolitano/projeto-adaptacao), developed in partnership with the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), provides technical support to help municipalities incorporate climate adaptation into urban planning instruments and processes.

Further, the [Climate Adaptation in Cities: Water-sensitive Urban Planning](https://www.ikibrasil.com/en/projects/climate-adaptation-in-cities-water-sensitive-urban-planning/) project, supported by Germany's International Climate Initiative (IKI) and implemented with UNEP, works across seven metropolitan regions – Belém, Belo Horizonte, Curitiba, Porto Alegre, Recife, Rio de Janeiro and Salvador. It seeks to strengthen planning and implementation of nature-based solutions for water-related climate risks by engaging national, state, metropolitan, municipal and community stakeholders.

International networks and partnerships also support urban climate action in Brazil through technical assistance, knowledge exchange and improved access to finance. These include, but are not limited to, [C40 Cities](https://www.c40.org/), [ICLEI](https://americadosul.iclei.org/), [UNEP](https://www.unep.org/), [GIZ](https://www.giz.de/en), the [Global Covenant of Mayors](https://www.globalcovenantofmayors.org/), the [CCFLA Brazil Local Hub](https://citiesclimatefinance.org/brazil-hub) and [WRI Brasil's Network for Financing Sustainable Infrastructure in Cities (Rede FISC)](https://www.wribrasil.org.br/projetos/rede-fisc).

Domestically, FNP's [Subnational Climate Finance Working Group](https://fnp.org.br/noticias/item/3812-gt-de-financiamento-climatico-subnacional-debate-acesso-a-recursos-para-cidades-brasileiras) also facilitates exchanges among municipalities on barriers and opportunities for accessing climate finance.
actions.enabledSummary: Brazil has developed experience in federally supported urban demonstrations, municipal capacity building and international partnerships. The opportunity is to institutionalise learning from these initiatives and connect capacity development with investment planning, financing and implementation across municipalities.

countryJourneysOverview.title: Country Journeys
countryJourneysOverview.introP1: The Country Journeys illustrate how national and subnational governments are developing multilevel approaches to mobilize finance and implement urban climate action. Each journey traces the evolution of a country's institutional and financing arrangements and maps relevant policies, programs and initiatives against the Toolkit's guidance, organized into five key Actions. The purpose of Country Journeys is to showcase the progress countries have made in developing multilevel climate finance and implementation approaches and the lessons others can draw. By highlighting countries’ progress, the CHAMP Toolkit aims to inspire peer learning and provide practical ideas that other countries can adapt to their own contexts.
countryJourneysOverview.submitText: We welcome contributions from national governments and partners to expand the Country Journeys and showcase diverse approaches to multilevel climate finance and implementation. If you would like to share your country's experience, please contact the CCFLA Secretariat at ccflasecretariat@cpiglobal.org.

roadmapPillars.title: Pillar 1: Strengthening multilevel climate governance with a view to enhance the visibility, role and contribution of sub-national actors
roadmapPillars.goal: CHAMP-endorsing countries have deepened their engagement with the CHAMP coalition, and the global climate governance architecture has strengthened its recognition of subnational governments as critical partners to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement.
roadmapPillars.leadResponsibility: Steering Group and Secretariat, with active engagement from CHAMP endorsing countries.
roadmapPillars.overview: Under this pillar, the CHAMP Steering Group works to deepen engagement with CHAMP endorsing countries, ensure subnational voices are heard more clearly in global climate decision making, seek greater recognition of the role of subnational governments across a targeted set of global climate governance instruments and reports and support transparent, country-led review processes.
roadmapPillars.transitionNote: Building on the global engagement and governance architecture advanced under Pillar 1, Pillar 2 focuses on the practical, country-level conditions needed to deliver multilevel climate action on the ground.

activities.title: Enhance multilevel climate dialogue
bullets: Convene an annual High-Level Political Dialogue bringing together national and subnational leaders from CHAMP-endorsing countries to showcase progress and drive global engagement and diplomacy [Secretariat].
Build formal links between CHAMP and other multilateral and sectoral initiatives to strengthen alignment and impact [Steering Group and Secretariat].

activities.title: Influence global climate governance instruments and reports
bullets: Secure strong recognition of multilevel partnerships as integral to effective climate action in the Global Implementation Accelerator (GIA) report [Steering Group].

Facilitate a positive response to the IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Cities (SR), highlighting the report's recognition of multilevel partnerships as a key enabler of climate action [Steering Group].

Advocate for the Second Global Stocktake (GST2) to reiterate the value of local and subnational actors as indispensable partners to national governments for implementing climate action [Steering Group].

Ensure Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) contain strengthened multilevel governance content that demonstrates intentional and strategic linkages between national and subnational levels [CHAMP-endorsing countries].
Foster connections with related initiatives and processes to mainstream local and regional dimensions, unlock synergies, and secure complementary, coordinated action

activities.title: Encourage transparent, voluntary country-led review processes
bullets: Provide guidance on integrating voluntary multilevel reviews into existing national reporting processes [Secretariat and CHAMP partners].
Leverage Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs) as a voluntary review of progress at national and subnational level on the implementation of CHAMP commitments [CHAMP-endorsing countries].

roadmapPillars.title: Pillar 2: Catalysing partnerships for local climate delivery
roadmapPillars.goal: CHAMP-endorsing countries have strengthened multilevel partnership mechanisms to ensure subnational priorities and efforts are integrated into the design, financing and delivery of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs).
roadmapPillars.leadResponsibility: Secretariat and CHAMP partners, with CHAMP-endorsing countries as primary implementers.
roadmapPillars.overview: Under this pillar, CHAMP-endorsing countries move from ambition to action, building the enabling conditions, partnerships and delivery mechanisms needed for effective multilevel climate implementation, including robust coordination mechanisms, integrated planning, and alignment between subnational priorities and national development policies.
roadmapPillars.transitionNote: Leveraging the enabling conditions, partnerships and delivery mechanisms advanced under Pillar 2, Pillar 3 works to unlock the investment flows needed to sustain long-term multilevel climate action at scale.

activities.title: Support enabling conditions for multilevel climate implementation
bullets: Seek to coordinate CHAMP partner support around country needs, with a view to ensuring technical assistance, capacity building and other cooperation are complementary and strategically aligned with CHAMP priorities where possible [Secretariat and NDC Partnership].

Where partner resources and mandates allow, provide targeted assistance to CHAMP endorsing countries to establish or strengthen coordination mechanisms, develop integrated implementation plans, and create a strong foundation for investment mobilisation [CHAMP partners].

activities.title: Ensure access to relevant data, knowledge and tools
bullets: Develop case studies, guidance, and other resources tailored to the multilevel implementation needs of CHAMP-endorsing countries and maintain a publicly accessible CHAMP knowledge hub, connecting with relevant content across partner-owned resource platforms [Secretariat and CHAMP partners].
Publish an annual CHAMP progress, impact and learnings report to demonstrate the value of multilevel partnerships and support informed decision-making [Secretariat].

activities.title: Facilitate knowledge exchange and good practice sharing
bullets: Convene peer exchanges for CHAMP-endorsing countries through dedicated CHAMP events and targeted participation at key international events to share experiences and practical approaches to implementation [Secretariat and CHAMP partners].

Support ongoing knowledge sharing across the CHAMP community to enhance collaboration and promote good practice and shared learning on multilevel climate governance and implementation [Secretariat and CHAMP partners].

roadmapPillars.title: Pillar 3: Scaling up and unlocking the means of implementation, including finance and investment, at the subnational level
roadmapPillars.goal: CHAMP-endorsing countries have established robust pathways to scale up and unlock subnational government access to climate finance, with subnational priorities integrated into national and global investment plans.
roadmapPillars.leadResponsibility: Steering Group, Secretariat and CHAMP partners, with CHAMP-endorsing countries as primary implementers.
roadmapPillars.overview: Under this pillar, CHAMP-endorsing countries move from planning to investment mobilisation by translating subnational climate priorities into investable projects, strengthening regulatory and institutional frameworks, and building reliable pathways for public and private finance to reach regional and local governments.

activities.title: Integrate subnational priorities into national climate finance strategies and investment plans
bullets: Facilitate coordination and knowledge exchange between CHAMP-endorsing countries and CHAMP partners on subnational climate finance strategies, engaging national finance ministries, planning agencies and other stakeholders to support integration of subnational priorities into national investment plans and sectoral policies [Secretariat and CHAMP partners].

activities.title: Enable a coordinated approach to project preparation
bullets: Convene project preparation providers, national government ministries and finance institutions with a view to developing coordinated national-level approaches to project development [Secretariat and CHAMP partners].

Where partner resources and mandates allow, provide capacity building and technical support for subnational project preparation in CHAMP-endorsing countries to strengthen the pipeline of bankable projects [CHAMP partners].

activities.title: Advocate for reform of finance institutions and climate funds
bullets: Develop reform proposals or recommendations for domestic and international development finance institutions, and vertical climate funds so that they better reflect the needs, opportunities and constraints of subnational governments [Steering Group and CHAMP partners].

Convene multi-stakeholder dialogues with domestic and international development finance institutions, and vertical climate funds to build consensus around reform needs and strengthen coordination on implementation [CHAMP partners].
Champion reform of domestic finance institutions and vertical climate funds within national policy processes to increase subnational access to climate finance [CHAMP-endorsing countries].

champPledges.title: Consult on national commitments and strategies
champPledges.shortDesc: Avenues for subnational action in mitigation and adaptation strategies.
champPledges.fullText: Consult with our respective subnational governments, as appropriate and applicable, to determine the avenues for subnational action to contribute to national mitigation and adaptation commitments and strategies, and their subsequent implementation and monitoring.

champPledges.title: Work collaboratively to unlock subnational opportunities
champPledges.shortDesc: Involving subnational governments in review, design, and consolidation.
champPledges.fullText: Work collaboratively with our respective subnational governments to unlock and realise mitigation and adaptation action opportunities at the subnational level by involving them, as appropriate and applicable, in the review, design, enhancement, consolidation and implementation of our national commitments and strategies.

champPledges.title: Inclusive institutional processes for enhanced NDCs
champPledges.shortDesc: Enabling subnational baseline info, targets and actions ahead of COP30.
champPledges.fullText: Create inclusive institutional and informal processes to enable subnational governments to contribute to further enhancing NDCs, where applicable, ahead of COP30 in 2025, and, where available and appropriate, integrate local and territorial baseline information, targets and actions for emissions mitigation and adaptation across all sectors and industries.

champPledges.title: Climate-related investment priorities & project preparation
champPledges.shortDesc: Directly driving subnational pipelines, finance mobilization, and project readiness.
champPledges.fullText: Include relevant subnational government projects (encompassing mitigation and adaptation) in climate-related investment priorities (including those directly and indirectly related to NDCs) and strive to help them secure the resources necessary from public and private financial institutions, as applicable, to begin or scale up implementation, including but not limited to supporting project preparation, pipeline development, aggregation of projects, new financial instruments or policy reform at local, national, regional and global levels as needed.

champPledges.title: Regular country-led reviews of progress
champPledges.shortDesc: National and subnational review processes to accelerate ambitious action.
champPledges.fullText: Undertake, as appropriate and applicable, regular, and inclusive country-led reviews of progress at national and subnational level around the implementation of CHAMP commitments through existing processes, which may include the Voluntary National Review process of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, with a view to ensure that national policy frameworks support and, where appropriate, can accelerate ambitious multilevel climate action.

champPledges.title: Global High Level Political Dialogue
champPledges.shortDesc: Sharing good practices and lessons learned with subnational leaders.
champPledges.fullText: Meet, amongst the endorsers of CHAMP, with representative subnational leaders, at a global High Level Political Dialogue on Multilevel Climate Action in the lead up to both COP29 and COP30 to share good practices and lessons learned in implementing the CHAMP commitments, to be compiled into a summary shared, among others, as a contribution to the Ministerial Meeting on Urbanization and Climate Change.
